circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for the concluding Formula One race of the season since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 designation. It serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix, alongside various supporting racing series and events.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and hosted the Austrian Grand Prix annually between 1970 and 1987. Following extensive modifications and a rebranding, the track resumed hosting the race from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, situated along Baku Boulevard, measuring approximately 6 kilometers per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before being rebranded for the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, which became the event's permanent designation.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various racing categories including GP2 Series, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance events, while featuring multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona is a 4. 657 km motorsport venue featuring a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodating over 140,000 spectators, the track regularly hosts major international racing events.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Belgium's Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit situated near the town of Spa in Wallonia, hosting the Belgian Grand Prix for Formula One. The track has maintained an almost continuous presence on the F1 calendar since 1985, with only two omissions in 2003 and 2006, tracing its motorsport heritage back to 1925 when it first staged a Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km street circuit that serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary role in motorsport's premier series, the venue has hosted various other racing championships including sportscar and open-wheel competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading District, is a Chinese motorsport venue that primarily hosted the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix alongside the Formula One event starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948 and was the venue for the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with other circuits for three decades, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, while the track also accommodates international motorcycle racing events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km permanent circuit that hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it debuted in 1986. Built in just eight months, a faster construction timeline than any contemporary Formula One venue, the track was developed as a compromise between plans for a Monaco-style street circuit and governmental preferences for a dedicated facility.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian race track constructed in 1922, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built circuit and only the third of its kind worldwide. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix almost continuously since 1949, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and rapid corners, and remains one of the select few circuits present throughout Formula One's entire calendar history.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track gained prominence as a mainstay fixture for both Formula One and Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street-based racing layout situated in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban environment. The track weaves past some of the region's most iconic destinations, including major casino resorts and the MSG Sphere, creating a unique racing venue integrated into the city's landscape.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit in Mexico City honoring two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three distinct eras, with the current continuous run beginning in 2015 on its present configuration, now officially titled the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds around 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the venue hosted its inaugural Grand Prix in 2022 and has since become the sport's home in South Florida, with the track also adapted for electric racing series beginning in 2025.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Monaco Grand Prix takes place on a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the contours of the harbour area. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, the track is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its primary location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to the Formula One calendar in 2021. The venue's partnership with Formula One concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Grade 1 racing facility situated north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, situated in São Paulo, Brazil, is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing venue that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The complex features additional amenities including a karting track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021, with Formula E competition commencing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Downtown Core and Kallang districts, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay waterfront for racing purposes.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing various driving skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR and motorcycle racing events. The venue has established itself as a premier destination for international motorsport, having previously attracted various racing series including IndyCar and sports car championships across multiple decades.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed 32 Grand Prix victories and two world championship titles during his 23-season career with Renault. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to have won both Formula One and World Endurance Championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, having secured eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team. He has established himself as a competitor in the sport's premier racing series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his motorsporting talent to the grid.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver has competed in Formula One for over a decade, securing ten race victories and finishing as championship runner-up on two occasions while previously driving for Mercedes. He currently races for Cadillac in the series.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Argentine driver Franco Colapinto currently races in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents his nation in the sport's premier motorseries.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines his endurance racing commitments in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory with AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Formula One driver of French and Algerian nationality who races for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Ferrari in Formula One. The driver holds an equal record of seven world championships alongside Michael Schumacher and leads in multiple statistical categories including race victories, front-row starts, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi after establishing himself through multiple team stints in the sport. Beyond his single-seater career, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, claiming victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Monaco-born Charles Leclerc drives for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured second place in the 2022 drivers' championship and accumulated nine race victories throughout his career spanning nine seasons.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also participating part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series for Trackhouse Racing. He previously had two separate stints in Formula One, racing from 2014-2020 and returning for the 2022-2024 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris represents Britain in Formula One racing, driving for McLaren where he secured the 2025 world championship title. The driver has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One. He previously achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Checo Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren, has secured nine Grand Prix victories during his four seasons in Formula One.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo is an Australian driver who competed in Formula One spanning 2011 to 2024, earning the nickname "the Honey Badger" during his 14-season career. He secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured seven race victories during his eight seasons competing in Formula One, currently racing for Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with Proton Competition in the LMGT3 category. Following a brief Formula One career spanning 2023 to 2024, he has transitioned to sports car racing, including previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian motorsport competitor who currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve role with both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He maintained a full-time racing position from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a backup capacity in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He holds the distinction of being the only Chinese-born driver to have participated in Formula One's premier championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has competed as Alpine since 2021, when Renault rebranded its works team to highlight its Alpine sports car division. Operating under various sponsorship arrangements, the team maintained factory support from Renault until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport following the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has entered Formula One multiple times throughout the sport's history, with the current incarnation operating as a British-registered team competing under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, has participated in every Formula One World Championship since 1950, making it both the sport's longest-running team and its most accomplished. The squad, colloquially referred to by their equine emblem reference, remains unmatched in longevity and competitive success throughout Formula One's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, debuting in the 2016 season with support from Toyota's racing division. Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role in 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who led the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering outfit, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, initially made its mark in endurance racing before transitioning to Formula One in 1993. During its three-decade stint in the championship, the team competed as an independent constructor through various iterations until ceasing operations in 2025, having started the fourth-most races of any constructor in the sport's history. Audi acquired the operation in 2024 to serve as the technical and competitive foundation for its entry into Formula One.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, competing under the Mastercard sponsorship banner. As a division of the McLaren Group, the team is ultimately controlled by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-AMG Petronas has been a fixture in Formula One since the 1950s, competing as a constructor and engine supplier across multiple eras. Based in Brackley and holding a German licence, the team has been jointly owned since 2022 by Mercedes-Benz, Ineos, and Toto Wolff in equal shares. The outfit, traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows," represents one of motorsport's most historically significant racing programmes.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of Red Bull GmbH's two teams, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as a second outfit within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of Red Bull's two racing operations. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit to Red Bull Racing under Austrian ownership.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian licence from a British headquarters, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and became one of two series entries controlled by Red Bull GmbH. Christian Horner served as team principal throughout the squad's two-decade history before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture, is a British Formula One constructor headquartered at Grove, Oxfordshire. The team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and has maintained its manufacturing and operational base on a substantial facility in southern England since its inception.
